elements.label: filter envelope peak frequency; depth adjusts from minus 96 to plus 96 semitones

designNotes.purpose: Deep four-operator FM sound design through a direct, compact workflow. Core working controls remain exposed; occasional construction tools expand horizontally.
designNotes.envelopes: One explicitly selected oscillator envelope, with three ghost curves, on a locked nonlinear time scale. Attack 0 ms–20 s; decay/release 1 ms–60 s; sustain −infinity–0 dB. Initial/peak and curvature are graph edits. Filter has one independent envelope in the same editor.
designNotes.looping: Attack/decay loop in free, tempo-fit and note-pitch-fit modes. Every cycle resets immediately to the envelope initial level, preserving cycle duration and shape. Only the envelope restarts, not oscillator phase. Note-off wins over a simultaneous loop reset and enters normal release from the pre-reset current level. There is no alternate restart option in the first iteration.
designNotes.host: 200 px height; left rail: power, device menu, bottom-up name, macros, modulators. Both panels open independently. Uniform square slots at two/three/four-high sizes, with additional columns after four. Full-unit presets include macros, mappings and nested chain.
designNotes.prototype: Buttons demonstrate named states; numeric inputs retain session text. Curve/partial edits are illustrative immediate preview states, not a native sound engine or freehand editor. Undo for real synthesis edits remains a native interaction requirement.
designNotes.reviewRefinements: Loop regions/readouts follow the selected A/D durations. Synced A/D fields show proportions, with cycle/rate captions and a shared 2 s note-off preview. Active curves render above ghosts. Default panels are closed; three slot content sizes, routing paths/feedback target, slider fills, glide and keyboard focus have explicit visual treatments. Filter levels use 0–100% and bipolar depth uses −96 to +96 semitones. All loop modes reset to initial; note-off takes priority. Oscillator letters are noninteractive, selected-point headers retain source identity, point values have more width, and four-high macro values sit beside their knob. Section, routing-choice and envelope-handle keyboard focus have explicit previews.
designNotes.sectionSelection: Click an oscillator section background to select its envelope. The colored left rectangle only enables/disables that oscillator. Filter section background selects its independent envelope; cutoff/resonance edits preserve selection. Section selection uses a blue outline/fill and keyboard focus, not duplicate letter/env buttons. Routing diagram itself opens a visual preset palette; there is no separate label or text selector.
designNotes.envelopeReadouts: Source-aware point names have a 96 px header region; exact values have 93 px and at least 9 px type. Common d/s and a/d/r curve abbreviations keep the header compact; full parameter names remain available as contextual help in native implementation.
designNotes.loopClarity: The first A/D cycle has a stronger tint. The graph shows a vertical reset-to-initial arrow and a second cycle, clipped at note-off if necessary. The held interval and repeat bracket run to note-off; release starts at the actual level reached within the repeated shape. Tempo/pitch examples whose note-off coincides with a cycle boundary release from the decay endpoint before a reset. All modes share the locked nonlinear time scale.
designNotes.filterEnvelope: Depth is -96 to +96 semitones, default 0 st. Cutoff shows the base frequency; env peak shows cutoff at the edited envelope peak level: base Hz × 2^(depth × peak/12), bounded by the supported filter range. The control normally shows Hz/kHz; precise entry temporarily shows semitones with the calculated frequency and range nearby. At 500 Hz with +24 st, 100% peak reads 2 kHz and 50% peak reads 1 kHz. Filter cutoff, resonance and env peak share one selection section. Device settings live in the host menu.
designNotes.compactness: The default host is 708 × 200 px. Keep the short oscillator tuning fields. The envelope uses compact source-aware point names (d/s and a/d/r curve) and a 93 px exact-value field. Core controls use two tight filter rows and value fields sized for their expected range. Settings and oscillator options open in a 168 px panel; the waveform editor retains 264 px. Precise-entry help is a transient popover, not a reserved blank row. Keyboard icons use a small key drawing.
